catholic-encyclopedia-1913-joseph-heinz:
Joseph Heinz was a Swiss court painter to Emperor Rudolf II. Born at Basle in 1564, he likely trained under Hans Bock and taught himself by copying Hans Holbein the younger. He lived in Rome from 1585 to 1587 and settled in Bohemia in 1591. At once he became court painter at Prague, though he soon returned to Rome to copy antiques for the emperor.

His portraits and landscapes were his best work, including the family portrait at Berne and Rudolf II at Vienna. His landscapes, often too green, were simple in design and showed his deep study of light. The Dresden Gallery holds his Rape of Proserpine, Lot and His Daughters, and Ecce Homo. He died near Prague in 1609.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-linz:
Linz is the Catholic diocese covering Upper Austria, with its seat in the city of Linz. Emperor Joseph II carved it out of the huge Diocese of Passau in the 1780s. He hoped to curb Passau's power inside his lands, and Pope Pius VI gave the plan his reluctant backing in 1784.

Count von Herberstein, once Passau's deputy in Vienna, became the first bishop, and the bull of erection followed in January 1785. At its start the diocese held 26 deaneries and 404 parishes. Its church life soon felt Joseph's sweeping reforms: old devotions were cut back, churches were closed, and monasteries were shut. Later bishops, schools, and church building fill out a long record of a young see finding its feet under a meddling state.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-mainz:
Mainz was a German town and bishopric in Hesse. It once held an archbishop who was also an elector of the empire. A Celtic settlement stood near the site centuries before Christ. Its church and secular weight grew with its early archbishops. They built monasteries and ranked high among spiritual princes.

In the investiture struggle its archbishops could not stay neutral. As a free imperial town, Mainz thrived on linen and wool along the Rhine. Rival claimants tore it in the Stiftsfehde of 1461 to 1463. The Thirty Years' War then hit it hard. A modern diocese later gathered pieces of Mainz, Worms, Speyer, and Metz. Rome once refused a bishop chosen by the chapter. The present diocese matches the Grand Duchy of Hesse, save three places under Limburg, and its Romanesque cathedral leads its churches.
